routes.name: Work
routes.change: Split opening with one featured AssetRounds preview; shorten duplicated case-study content; retain all existing work; add the Fieldwork design desk.
routes.acceptance: The opening shows real website work; each concept can be inspected; the desk explains a design decision; inquiry remains easy to find.

routes.name: Services
routes.change: Add a concise evidence panel to each of the existing Build / Improve / Ongoing groups. Keep the seven service cards, prices and group anchors.
routes.acceptance: A visitor can distinguish a new website, a repair and ongoing help without using an interaction or opening an example.

routes.name: Web design
routes.change: The AssetRounds preview is already directly after the introduction. Improve its framing and explanation in place; add one quiet design-desk link.
routes.acceptance: Exactly one featured example; current writing example, starting price and primary inquiry remain available.

routes.name: Website redesign
routes.change: Add an illustrative Keep / Improve / Move page map beside the existing redesign explanation.
routes.acceptance: The map explains content and address decisions without implying a completed client redesign.

routes.name: Contractor websites
routes.change: Pair the actual Northline concept capture with one short note connecting services, project evidence and an estimate request.
routes.acceptance: The example is labeled fictional and links to the existing concept; trade-specific information remains more prominent than decoration.

routes.name: Website reviews & fixes
routes.change: Refine auditSample() in place: show the existing Northline before/after enlarged-text repair and its Finding / Action / Check explanation.
routes.acceptance: Preserve the local-preview provenance and same-width/text-size explanation; distinguish screenshot evidence from the separate two-fix record.

routes.name: Website add-ons
routes.change: Show the existing inquiry tracker demonstration near the custom-tools category.
routes.acceptance: Caption explains that the browser demo does not send email or connect to a live customer system; prices and scope remain readable.

routes.name: Website care
routes.change: Show approved hours/photo change → updated page → check record, based on the current illustrative care scenario.
routes.acceptance: Customer-supplied information and approval remain explicit; the visual does not imply autonomous updates or new package inclusions.

routes.name: Monthly SEO
routes.change: Refine the existing monthly example into customer question → researched page improvement → published page and checks.
routes.acceptance: Research, writing, publication and checks remain parts of ONE agreed improvement. Keep the existing sample and real studio page-planning link; no invented outcomes.

routes.name: Process
routes.change: Add compact proposal, design-review and handoff artifacts beside the matching stages. Retain the timing panel and current sequence.
routes.acceptance: Customer/studio responsibilities, payment triggers and stage anchors remain intact; illustrations do not duplicate or renumber milestones.

routes.name: Homepage
routes.change: Add one contextual “Try a design direction” link near the existing concept examples, pointing to /work/#design-desk.
routes.acceptance: Living city, section order, existing AssetRounds preview, primary actions, navigation and footer retain their behavior.

findings.finding: The approved image shows the intended composition, but invents some artwork and a mini-site menu.
findings.resolution: Use its hierarchy, palette and rhythm. Use actual project captures and the existing Fieldwork drawing in production; omit fake preview navigation.

findings.finding: V1 says to move the Web Design example earlier, although it already follows the intro. Work also has a separate full case study.
findings.resolution: Refine Web Design in place; use one compact Work feature and send detailed inspection to the existing case-study page.

findings.finding: V1 lists breakpoints but does not establish the reading order or space budget of the desk.
findings.resolution: Define phone-first hero and desk orders; show the result immediately after its controls; put explanations underneath.

findings.finding: assetRoundsPreview() is used on Home and Web Design; assetRoundsCase() is used on Work and its detail page. Process milestones are also shared.
findings.resolution: Use explicit opt-in variants or separate landing components. Keep current defaults for unmodified callers.

findings.finding: The mockup can be interpreted as filtering tabs. Existing Work categories are anchor links.
findings.resolution: Keep ordinary in-page links, visible content and working fragment URLs. No filter, horizontal swipe requirement or tab semantics.

findings.finding: The original visual direction is strong but could still produce an attractive wall of examples.
findings.resolution: Each example answers one visitor question, carries one sentence about a design decision and offers one clear inspection link.

findings.finding: A generic “all six combinations work” misses resize, failed initialization, link carry-through and visual changes below the fold.
findings.resolution: Add a state matrix, real phone review, zoom/reflow, current source baseline, link and asset checks, and an evidence checklist.

findings.finding: The plan can be built as one large change before the new visual system is proven.
findings.resolution: Prove Work and one service group first; review a reusable component sheet; then adapt details and Process.
